title: Stop Trusting npm Scans: Run Untrusted Packages in an Isolated AWS Sandbox
why_read: A concrete and well-motivated approach to catching supply-chain attacks in npm packages by actually executing installs in a sandbox.
analysis: The core insight here is sound: static scanners that only read package manifests and source code miss malicious behavior that only triggers during actual installation, like a postinstall script calling out to download and run further code. The author built a tool that runs npm install inside a disposable AWS CodeBuild sandbox and inspects the real build log for dangerous behavior like piping curl output to bash. This is a practical, well-scoped solution to a well-known supply chain security gap, and the architecture (isolated, disposable execution environment) is a sensible pattern others can adopt. Worth reading for anyone concerned about dependency security in JavaScript ecosystems.
